newsitem.title: USA: Kansas wheat needs moisture, condition stable.
newsitem.headline: Kansas wheat needs moisture, condition stable.

text.p: Kansas soil moisture supplies continued to decline during the week ended Sunday and moisture was needed for the wheat crop, the state's agricultural statistics service said in its weekly crop report.
Condition ratings for winter wheat were nearly unchanged from the previous week with the crop rated 11 percent excellent, 44 good, 30 fair, 11 poor and four very poor.

Statewide, 56 percent of the wheat had headed, the same as last year and compared with the 61 average. Cases of Russian wheat aphids, greenbugs, wheat streak mosaic, barley yellow dwarf and leaf rust were reported in the wheat.
Corn planting was 90 percent complete versus 95 last year and the 81 average. The crop was rated nine percent excellent, 68 good, 21 fair and two poor to very poor.
Sorghum planting was 20 percent complete versus 15 last year and the 13 average.
Soybean planting was 35 percent complete, ahead of 12 last year and the 14 average.

Pastures were nine percent excellent, 58 good, 28 fair and five poor. Topsoil moisture was seven percent very short, 37 short, 55 adequate and one percent surplus. Subsoil moisture was rated three percent very short, 17 short, 79 adequate and one surplus.
